Minsk Mazowiecki Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mińsk Mazowiecki, Poland

Demolished. Mińsk Mazowiecki's original Jewish cemetery, likely established at the beginning of the 19th century (no later than 1822), covered 0.8 hectares by the late 19th century, walled and adjacent to an Evangelical cemetery to the north (see the Mińsk Mazowiecki New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller Hasidic and Holocaust history). It probably closed in the 1870s, with occasional burials continuing until 1883, coinciding with the neighboring Evangelical cemetery's own closure and the 1866-1867 Warsaw-Terespol Railway construction that expanded the city westward. A 1923 letter from nearby property owners complained the long-unused cemetery obstructed pedestrian traffic on Sewerynów Street. A school (now the Economic School Complex) was built on the site in the early 1960s.
